8:1.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَنفَالِۖ قُلِ ٱلۡأَنفَالُ لِلَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِۖ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَصۡلِحُواْ ذَاتَ بَيۡنِكُمۡۖ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
8:1.en: They ask thee (O Muhammad) of the spoils of war. Say: The spoils of war belong to Allah and the messenger, so keep your duty to Allah, and adjust the matter of your difference, and obey Allah and His messenger, if ye are (true) believers

8:60.ar: وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُم مَّا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُم مِّن قُوَّةࣲ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلۡخَيۡلِ تُرۡهِبُونَ بِهِۦ عَدُوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ وَءَاخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُهُمۡۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تُظۡلَمُونَ
8:60.en: Make ready for them all thou canst of (armed) force and of horses tethered, that thereby ye may dismay the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others beside them whom ye know not. Allah knoweth them. Whatsoever ye spend in the way of Allah it will be repaid to you in full, and ye will not be wronged

8:2.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُهُۥ زَادَتۡهُمۡ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
8:2.en: They only are the (true) believers whose hearts feel fear when Allah is mentioned, and when His revelations are recited unto them they increase their faith, and who trust in their Lord

8:3.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
8:3.en: Who establish worship and spend of that We have bestowed on them

8:4.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ حَقࣰّ اۚ لَّهُمۡ دَرَجَٰتٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ وَرِزۡقࣱ كَرِيمࣱ‏
8:4.en: Those are they who are in truth believers. For them are grades (of honour) with their Lord, and pardon, and a bountiful provision

gMs-YF33msw.speaker: adnan
gMs-YF33msw.speaker_note: Single speaker throughout; refers to 'my series', his annual pre-Ramadan khutbahs on this minbar, his own household, and London organizations (Hikma). Matches the sheikh's Al-Anfal series.
gMs-YF33msw.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 2: Materialism
gMs-YF33msw.one_line: Opening Surah Al-Anfal as the Quran's 'laws of victory': the first law is to beat materialism, the surplus wealth that nearly spoiled Badr.
gMs-YF33msw.summary: He meant to open his new series on Surah Al-Anfal, the 'laws of victory', but begins with two months of war in Gaza and his bewilderment that even local MPs and mayors cannot bring themselves to ask for a ceasefire. His guess at what they fear, money and position, becomes the bridge into the surah. He explains where Al-Anfal sits in the Quran's thematic sequence, why a short surah of laws follows the seven long ones, and that its name means 'the extra': surplus wealth nobody actually needs. The surah opens with the Companions quarrelling over the spoils of Badr, and he tells how Sa'd was made to return a famous sword three times. If greed could almost spoil the greatest victory in Muslim history, it can spoil any community or any person. He warns young people how a rising standard of living quietly turns wants into needs until no time is left to serve, and cites the Prophet's fear not of poverty but of worldly abundance. The call is not to be poor but to own money rather than be owned by it: cut your standard of living, fund Muslim organizations and the masjid, and centralize community finances so Muslims in Canada have strength and a voice.

outline.heading: Politicians who cannot ask for a ceasefire
outline.gist: He means to start the series but cannot leave Gaza aside. He loves Canada, yet even local MPs and mayors will not simply ask that civilians stop being killed after 60 days of weekly protests by their own constituents. How deep does this power run?

outline.heading: What are they afraid of?
outline.gist: He wants to know what they fear: wealth, a job, money. He had assumed integrity would win over comfort at the sight of children buried under the rubble of their homes.

outline.heading: The pause as a test of memory
outline.gist: The series is not a distraction from the cause. The week-long pause may have been designed to see whether people forget and lose momentum, so advocacy must return more intensely than at the start.

outline.heading: The Quran is sequenced by topic
outline.gist: The first ten juz hold nine surahs, seven of them long, with a ten-page surah in their midst. It does not fit a sequence by length because the order is by topic: the first seven surahs set out purpose, values, covenant and relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: A short surah of laws
outline.gist: Then come the laws for success: how to maintain a nation, its relations inside and out, and keep its head above water. Laws are kept short, which is why the surah is shorter than those around it. Its first law ties back to wealth.

outline.heading: Al-Anfal: the extra
outline.gist: Anfal is one of the words for the spoils of war, alongside others such as fay. Its root is the same as nafl prayer: something extra that you do not need to stay alive.

outline.heading: Named after the danger
outline.gist: The surah is named after the number one problem because the Quran cares most about what not to do: there are many good things to do, but some things will sink your ship.

outline.heading: Revealed over the spoils of Badr
outline.gist: Ubadah ibn al-Samit narrates that the surah came down after Badr, when the people of Badr admit their conduct over the captured spoils was not good.

outline.heading: The sword of Sa'd
outline.gist: Sa'd brought the Prophet a famous sword he had won in a duel and asked to keep it; three times he was told to take it back to where it came from. He obeyed, but something of materialism was there.

outline.heading: To ruin anything, add materialism
outline.gist: Get people interested in money and profit and watch: this ruins communal aspirations, social work and individuals. He turns to the young, for whom money is not yet a priority.

outline.heading: How wants quietly become needs
outline.gist: If you are not careful, comfort and leisure grow, habits that cost money become norms, the baseline of what you need rises, and job security and earning take over until no time is left to volunteer or care about the world.

outline.heading: The standard of life you choose
outline.gist: People who make millions feel they are barely getting by, because it is all about the standard of life you set for yourself. Beware the extra you do not need: it almost ruined Badr.

outline.heading: Greed nearly spoiled Badr
outline.gist: Nothing in Muslim history compares to Badr, yet a little greed nearly ruined it, from men well below the poverty line. The Quran answers that the spoils belong to Allah and His Messenger, so be mindful of your Lord.

outline.heading: The Prophet feared wanting more, not poverty
outline.gist: Purify what is inside you and between you. The Prophet said it is not poverty he feared for them but takathur, which linguistically means the desire for more.

outline.heading: Want and need are not the same
outline.gist: Every year before Ramadan he repeats that what we want and what we need differ; you can live happily on far less unless you insist you deserve more. He warns the young about the lure of money.

outline.heading: Not a call to poverty: two treatments of wealth
outline.gist: The wealthy people he knows talk only of trips and money, little of what wealth could do. The surah does not want you poor: it treats wealth in two ways, do not be materialistic, and spend in the way of Allah, which is never lost.

outline.heading: Own your money
outline.gist: Make as much money as you can, but own it rather than letting it own you, and use it for the ummah and the people around you. The surah is named the extra, not money, because wealth itself is not the problem.

outline.heading: If they were not in need, what are we?
outline.gist: The Companions were in dire need, yet Allah called what they wanted extra. His own house has food for a month, a car and a home that do the job; he cannot comprehend how Allah sees our state.

outline.heading: The true believers
outline.gist: The surah goes on to describe the true believers: hearts that tremble at the mention of their Lord, faith that grows when the verses are recited, reliance on Him, prayer, and spending from what He provides. They have high ranks and a generous provision.

outline.heading: Abu Ubaidah returns with the wealth of Bahrain
outline.gist: The poor Ansar stood quietly after Fajr hoping for the money. The Prophet gave them glad tidings but said he feared not their poverty but that the world would be opened to them and destroy them as it destroyed those before.

outline.heading: The nafs is a black hole
outline.gist: This concept is central to the deen: no matter how much wealth you throw into the nafs it devours more, raising the standard, the work and the neglect of others.

outline.heading: A traveller's provision; put money where our mouths are
outline.gist: We are told to be generous, not poor: take from this world only the provision of a traveller. If the ummah hopes for change it must put its wealth where its mouth is; masajid that are not funded eventually close.

outline.heading: Financial centralization: a community, not a population
outline.gist: As long as we chase the extra, the ummah will suffer. Wealth has to go into projects that give strength and a voice; he has argued for financial centralization so a community is not just a population.

outline.heading: Organizations on pathetic budgets
outline.gist: Managed wealth gets representatives to represent us and protects Muslims in their jobs. NCCM and Hikma locally run on pathetic budgets, yet we expect them to reach politicians, and we want masajid to serve us without giving.

outline.heading: Without properly managed wealth there is no strength
outline.gist: To prevent this from happening again, Muslims as minorities in the West need strength, and without properly managed wealth there is none. Otherwise khutbahs repeat with no change until people stop coming.

outline.heading: Question your standard of life: the first law
outline.gist: Go back to the way of our ancestors: go home and question your standard of living, live on less and put more into the community. This is the first law of victory; without it the rest are hardly worth sharing, which is why the surah is named after it.

outline.heading: Not over until rights are returned
outline.gist: Even if a ceasefire comes, temporary or longer, it is not over until rights are returned to the oppressed and persecuted, and that must stay on our radar for the rest of our lives.

themes.note: Al-Anfal is named after surplus wealth because that is the main danger to any success. He traces how a rising standard of living turns wants into needs and insists Islam asks you to own your money, not be owned by it.

themes.note: Financial centralization is what turns a population into a community: funding the masjid, education and representation so Muslims are protected and heard.

themes.note: Addressed to the young: money is not their focus yet, but unchecked habits and comfort slowly raise the baseline until wealth consumes their time and their capacity to serve.

themes.note: The Companions admit their conduct over the spoils of Badr was poor; Sa'd is made to return a prized sword, showing greed can touch even the best generation.

themes.note: The Quran's order is thematic: the seven long surahs set out purpose and covenant, and the short Al-Anfal follows as a book of laws for keeping a nation afloat.

themes.note: Materialism is treated in two ways in the surah: do not be materialistic, and spend what you earn in Allah's way, which will be repaid in full.

themes.note: The surah's first command after the spoils is to be mindful of Allah and purify what is inside you and between you; the desire for more must be removed from the soul.

39:23.ar: ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡحَدِيثِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مُّتَشَٰبِهࣰ ا مَّثَانِيَ تَقۡشَعِرُّ مِنۡهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُمۡ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمۡ وَقُلُوبُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡ هَادٍ
39:23.en: Allah hath (now) revealed the fairest of statements, a Scripture consistent, (wherein promises of reward are) paired (with threats of punishment), whereat doth creep the flesh of those who fear their Lord, so that their flesh and their hearts soften to Allah's reminder. Such is Allah's guidance, wherewith He guideth whom He will. And him whom Allah sendeth astray, for him there is no guide

39:24.ar: أَفَمَن يَتَّقِي بِوَجۡهِهِۦ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ وَقِيلَ لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ ذُوقُواْ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡسِبُونَ
39:24.en: Is he then, who will strike his face against the awful doom upon the Day of Resurrection (as he who doeth right)? And it will be said unto the wrong-doers: Taste what ye used to earn

39:25.ar: كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
39:25.en: Those before them denied, and so the doom came on them whence they knew not

39:26.ar: فَأَذَاقَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخِزۡيَ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَكۡبَرُۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
39:26.en: Thus Allah made them taste humiliation in the life of the world, and verily the doom of the Hereafter will be greater if they did but know

95:4.ar: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ فِيٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمࣲ‏
95:4.en: Surely We created man of the best stature

95:5.en: Then we reduced him to the lowest of the low

5:48.ar: وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَمُهَيۡمِنًا عَلَيۡهِۖ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَهُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡ عَمَّا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ لِكُلࣲّ جَعَلۡنَا مِنكُمۡ شِرۡعَةࣰ وَمِنۡهَاجࣰ اۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ فِي مَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۖ فَٱسۡتَبِقُواْ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ فِيهِ تَخۡتَلِفُونَ
5:48.en: And unto thee have We revealed the Scripture with the truth, confirming whatever Scripture was before it, and a watcher over it. So judge between them by that which Allah hath revealed, and follow not their desires away from the truth which hath come unto thee. For each We have appointed a divine law and a traced-out way. Had Allah willed He could have made you one community. But that He may try you by that which He hath given you (He hath made you as ye are). So vie one with another in good works. Unto Allah ye will all return, and He will then inform you of that wherein ye differ

3:3.ar: نَزَّلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلَ
3:3.en: He hath revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture with truth, confirming that which was (revealed) before it, even as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel

4:82.ar: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَۚ وَلَوۡ كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ غَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ ٱخۡتِلَٰفࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا
4:82.en: Will they not then ponder on the Qur'an? If it had been from other than Allah they would have found therein much incongruity

39:9.ar: أَمَّنۡ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ سَاجِدࣰ ا وَقَآئِمࣰ ا يَحۡذَرُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ وَيَرۡجُواْ رَحۡمَةَ رَبِّهِۦۗ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
39:9.en: Is he who payeth adoration in the watches of the night, prostrate and standing, bewaring of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, (to be accounted equal with a disbeliever)? Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Are those who know equal with those who know not? But only men of understanding will pay heed

13:28.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَطۡمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَا بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطۡمَئِنُّ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ
13:28.en: Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest

16:97.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَنُحۡيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰۖ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:97.en: Whosoever doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, him verily we shall quicken with good life, and We shall pay them a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do

16:118.ar: وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمۡنَا مَا قَصَصۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَمَا ظَلَمۡنَٰهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
16:118.en: And unto those who are Jews We have forbidden that which We have already related unto thee. And We wronged them not, but they were wont to wrong themselves

XilTqNrnKww.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Az-Zumar (39:23-26)
XilTqNrnKww.one_line: The Quran as the best way of life: an ordered, consistent, all-covering Book, khashyah that moves into action, and shielding oneself with one's face.
XilTqNrnKww.summary: Allah sent down the best speech, meaning the best way of life, since only the Creator knows what is good for us. 'A Book' means an organized message with chapters and aims, which is why he teaches surahs by their themes; the large classical tafsirs are reference compilations, not reading for laypeople, and while non-Arabs are excused, Arabs who cannot connect with their own Book have no excuse and should learn grammar before offering reflections. The Quran is consistent with itself and earlier scriptures, and moves across stories, values, belief and law to cover all of life. Khashyah combines fear of His justice, reverence and love; for such people a meaning passes from the mind to the heart and makes the skin shiver, then skin and heart soften into obeying it, otherwise tears in prayer are followed by injustice at home. Sincerity means following no one's word unconditionally except Allah's. Verses 24-26 close a chain of comparisons: the one who shields himself from punishment with his face. Obeying Allah is not pain now for reward later but a good life here and Paradise after, so choosing disgrace in both worlds makes no sense; the Prophet grieved over those who refused, even praying over Ibn Ubayy.

outline.heading: The best speech: the best way of life
outline.gist: Only the Creator knows what serves us; we were made His stewards, and serving what was created to serve us is a reversal.

outline.heading: 'A Book' means an ordered message
outline.gist: Kitab is a message with chapters and aims, as Sahih al-Bukhari is divided into books; the Quran is not a random string of verses.

outline.heading: Each surah has its own issue
outline.gist: The early Arabs grasped the distinct themes naturally, as one does not explain the air one breathes, so they did not spell them out.

outline.heading: What the great tafsir works were for
outline.gist: Al-Qurtubi, al-Tabari and al-Razi compiled every report and linguistic detail as a reference; laypeople reading them get lost.

outline.heading: A surah as an enclosing wall
outline.gist: Allah said 'a Book', not a narration; each surah walls off verses with their own subject.

outline.heading: Arabs have no excuse
outline.gist: Non-Arabs who cannot understand are excused, but a quarter of Muslims know Arabic and still do not connect with their Book.

outline.heading: Learn the tools before reflecting
outline.gist: Take courses in grammar and morphology and listen to the commentators; reflections that the language cannot bear are not acceptable.

outline.heading: Consistent with itself and earlier scriptures
outline.gist: Mutashabih: its teachings never contradict each other and confirm and oversee the Torah and Gospel.

outline.heading: Mathani: covering all of life
outline.gist: It moves between stories, values, belief, law, the heart, the individual and society, leaving nothing we need.

outline.heading: Fearing His justice, not injustice
outline.gist: From people we fear harm; from Allah we fear being treated with bare justice, and need His extra grace to be saved.

outline.heading: Reverence and love complete khashyah
outline.gist: Khashyah is not a synonym of fear: it joins fear of just punishment with reverence and love.

outline.heading: Shivering skin: meaning reaching the body
outline.gist: A soft, cleansed heart receives the idea from the mind and produces a feeling that reaches the body.

outline.heading: Then they soften into obedience
outline.gist: Without this step religion becomes spiritual singing followed by beating wives and eating haram; softening means doing what Allah asks.

outline.heading: Only Allah's word is followed without question
outline.gist: Do not sell your mind, heart or limbs to anyone; this is what sincerity means.

outline.heading: Take from me what agrees with the Book
outline.gist: Every companion and great scholar told people to reject his word if it contradicted Allah's, whatever the size of his turban.

outline.heading: That is Allah's guidance
outline.gist: The companions lived the Quran; asked about the Prophet's character, Aisha said it was the Quran.

outline.heading: Sincerity is given, so ask for it
outline.gist: The surah tastes these meanings so you apply what you can and ask Allah to bring you the rest.

outline.heading: Verses 24-26 recited
outline.gist: Shielding with the face, those before them punished unawares, and disgrace in this world.

outline.heading: A chain of comparisons
outline.gist: The devout night worshipper, the one due punishment, the opened chest, and now the one shielding with his face.

outline.heading: Shielding yourself with your face
outline.gist: Everyone protects the face first because it holds the senses; this one meets the punishment with it.

outline.heading: Not pleasure now and pain later
outline.gist: Disobedience offers yourself to punishment; if obedience meant a miserable life one could argue, but that is not the equation.

outline.heading: A good life here and there
outline.gist: Obedience brings tranquillity, contentment and a good life now and the highest Paradise after; even an unbeliever with sense chooses honour over baseness.

outline.heading: He teaches you to shield yourself
outline.gist: Protect yourself from the Fire even with half a date; Allah gives the recipe, and only ignorance, pride and heedlessness lead one to refuse.

outline.heading: Taste what you earned
outline.gist: The wrongdoers wronged themselves first; Allah did not wrong them.

outline.heading: I want good for you and you want harm for yourself
outline.gist: Those before them also denied; at Hunayn a new Muslim hid a dagger to kill the Prophet, who told him this and accepted his repentance.

outline.heading: He prayed over Ibn Ubayy
outline.gist: Despite all his harm, the Prophet shrouded him in his cloak and said he would ask forgiveness more than seventy times if it would help.

outline.heading: Disgrace in this world
outline.gist: Khizy is a fall from rank before people's eyes so they gloat; the punishment of the Hereafter is greater.

outline.heading: No balance between the two paths
outline.gist: One road is happy in both worlds and the other miserable in both; the other only glitters from afar, and sincerity is the clarity to see it.

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Now Korah was of Moses' folk, but he oppressed them; and We gave him so much treasure that the stores thereof would verily have been a burden for a troop of mighty men. When his own folk said unto him: Exult not; lo! Allah loveth not the exultant

28:77.ar: وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
28:77.en: But seek the abode of the Hereafter in that which Allah hath given thee and neglect not thy portion of the world, and be thou kind even as Allah hath been kind to thee, and seek not corruption in the earth; lo! Allah loveth not corrupters

28:78.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عِندِيٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَهۡلَكَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مَنۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُ قُوَّةࣰ وَأَكۡثَرُ جَمۡعࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
28:78.en: He said: I have been given it only on account of knowledge I possess. Knew he not that Allah had destroyed already of the generations before him men who were mightier than him in strength and greater in respect of following? The guilty are not questioned of their sins

28:79.ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فِي زِينَتِهِۦۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا يَٰلَيۡتَ لَنَا مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
28:79.en: Then went he forth before his people in his pomp. Those who were desirous of the life of the world said: Ah, would that we had the like of what hath been given unto Korah! Lo! he is lord of rare good fortune

28:80.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ وَيۡلَكُمۡ ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ لِّمَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ
28:80.en: But those who had been given knowledge said: Woe unto you! The reward of Allah for him who believeth and doeth right is better, and only the steadfast will obtain it

28:81.ar: فَخَسَفۡنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةࣲ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنتَصِرِينَ
28:81.en: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling-place. Then he had no host to help him against Allah, nor was he of those who can save themselves

28:82.ar: وَأَصۡبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوۡاْ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَمۡسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيۡكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُۖ لَوۡلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَاۖ وَيۡكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
28:82.en: And morning found those who had coveted his place but yesterday crying: Ah, welladay! Allah enlargeth the provision for whom He will of His slaves and straiteneth it (for whom He will). If Allah had not been gracious unto us He would have caused it to swallow us (also). Ah, welladay! the disbelievers never prosper

28:83.ar: تِلۡكَ ٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ نَجۡعَلُهَا لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُرِيدُونَ عُلُوࣰّ ا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فَسَادࣰ اۚ وَٱلۡعَٰقِبَةُ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
28:83.en: As for that Abode of the Hereafter We assign it unto those who seek not oppression in the earth, nor yet corruption. The sequel is for those who ward off (evil)

29:39.ar: وَقَٰرُونَ وَفِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا كَانُواْ سَٰبِقِينَ
29:39.en: And Korah, Pharaoh and Haman! Moses came unto them with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty), but they were boastful in the land. And they were not winners (in the race)

40:24.ar: إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَقَٰرُونَ فَقَالُواْ سَٰحِرࣱ كَذَّابࣱ‏

B1pswrMNxC4.title: Quranic Stories: The Story of Qarun
B1pswrMNxC4.one_line: Qarun, Musa's cousin and early follower, let wealth and proximity to power make him vain until he sold out and lost everything.
B1pswrMNxC4.summary: The sheikh presents Qarun's story in Surat al-Qasas as unique in the Quran: a man from Musa's own people, his cousin and once a core follower, who ends up listed beside Pharaoh and Haman. Talented and ambitious, Qarun built a fortune with his people's support, and Pharaoh, seeking to weaken Musa, flattered his ego and drew him into the ruling elite. The sheikh uses him as the Quran's example of vanity, one of four diseases of the heart, and asks whether our values are constants or variables that shift with wealth and status, contrasting the Prophet, who stayed the same in persecution and in power. He explains the advice Qarun's people gave: farah here means vain exultation rather than happiness, and wealth should be used for the Hereafter, shared as Allah shared with you, and kept from corruption. Qarun's reply that he earned it through his own knowledge reveals his heart: he did work hard, but by crediting himself and never saying alhamdulillah he judged his own effort instead of leaving that to Allah. When he paraded his wealth, worldly onlookers envied him, while the knowledgeable held firm. After the earth swallowed him, literally or gradually, the envious realised their mistake. The lesson is to let nothing change the humble, decent person you were.

outline.heading: A story with no parallel
outline.gist: Unlike most Quranic stories, Qarun's has no similar story elsewhere.

outline.heading: Qarun beside Pharaoh and Haman
outline.gist: Elsewhere the Quran groups him with Pharaoh and Haman, as if he were simply one of their servants.

outline.heading: He was of the people of Musa
outline.gist: Musa's first cousin and once a committed member of his core group, intelligent and from humble roots.

outline.heading: When the story took place
outline.gist: A minority place it after the crossing of the sea, but the Quran's pairing of him with Pharaoh suggests it happened in Egypt before.

outline.heading: A fortune built on his people's support
outline.gist: Bani Israel were proud of their successful businessman and helped him grow, until he turned on them.

outline.heading: Musa as the unifying leader
outline.gist: A divided people found unity in Musa's character; movements without leaders go nowhere.

outline.heading: Pharaoh plays on his ambition
outline.gist: Threatening his business and flattering him that he had outgrown Musa, Pharaoh pulled him to his side.

outline.heading: Qarun as the Quran's story of vanity
outline.gist: Among the four diseases of the heart, each with its Quranic story, Qarun is the example of vanity.

outline.heading: The slow shift of his narrative
outline.gist: Like Muslim leaders today who offer only toothless, watered-down statements, Qarun's speech and loyalty gradually changed.

outline.heading: Are your values constants or variables?
outline.gist: The enduring question is whether wealth and status change your ethics and basic decency.

outline.heading: The Prophet stayed the same
outline.gist: Whether persecuted or ruler of Arabia, the Prophet's humility and manner never changed.

outline.heading: Qarun failed his one test
outline.gist: Money changed how he spoke to and saw his people; watching a hero fall hurts.

outline.heading: Keys too heavy for a band of strong men
outline.gist: Even the keys to his treasures were a burden for a group of strong men.

outline.heading: Do not exult: farah as vanity
outline.gist: Musa sent others to advise him; in Quranic usage farah means vain self-satisfaction, not happiness.

outline.heading: Seek the Hereafter and do good as Allah did good to you
outline.gist: Enjoy wealth but invest it for the Hereafter, show ihsan to others and avoid the corruption now mixed into his wealth.

outline.heading: The elite's narrative
outline.gist: Joining the one percent, he adopted the view that people must be controlled and always want more, a narrative found here as much as in the Middle East.

outline.heading: I was given it through my own knowledge
outline.gist: He did work hard, and that deserves respect from others, but seeing himself that way showed his ego had swallowed him.

outline.heading: The nafs hears what it fears
outline.gist: No one told him he was simply handed his wealth; his ego filtered the advice to protect his money.

outline.heading: No alhamdulillah
outline.gist: Even crooks write that it is from their Lord; he never attributed anything to Allah, while the believer credits every achievement to Him.

outline.heading: Vanity is judging your own effort
outline.gist: Work hard but let Allah judge how well you did; your intelligence and grit are His creation.

outline.heading: Allah destroyed stronger men before him
outline.gist: Criminals need no questioning; the Prophet consoled himself with Musa's patience, and Qarun went as far as accepting the killing of his people's children.

outline.heading: He comes out in his finery
outline.gist: He paraded his power before Musa's followers, and those who secretly wanted the dunya wished they had what he had.

outline.heading: Al-Qasas: appearances mislead
outline.gist: Every story in the surah shows a scene you would misjudge, so stop judging people's stories; Qarun would have been better off never rich.

outline.heading: Let nothing change you
outline.gist: Those given knowledge said Allah's reward is better; only the patient can stand their ground.

outline.heading: The earth swallows him
outline.gist: Most hold it was a sudden event; others read it as losing wealth, status and supporters over time.

outline.heading: The envious realise their error
outline.gist: Allah gives and withholds wealth regardless of His love; the final abode is for those who seek neither exaltation nor corruption.

outline.heading: What he could have been
outline.gist: He could have crossed the sea with Musa and stood by him.

DjqxjEhs0es.title: Surat As-Saff, Part 2 (Verses 5-6)
DjqxjEhs0es.one_line: As-Saff 5-6: Musa's "why do you hurt me", accepting Islam as it is, and carrying the legacy forward as Isa did.
DjqxjEhs0es.summary: He continues the surah's social contract through two prophets. Musa asks his people why they hurt him while knowing he is Allah's messenger; their cutting of corners was a personal injury because failing your share of a collective harms every member, as on a sports team. Small, diluted shortfalls add up until the whole ummah suffers, so each person must work out what they can contribute. The Israelites heard and refused, then haggled to have commands reduced, and Allah let their hearts deviate. The third clause of the contract is accepting Islam as it is rather than as you would like it: you may struggle, fall short and ask for time and help, but you may not rewrite the law, as with the Sabbath ruse or demanding to bring alcohol into the masjid. Only qualified scholars can reinterpret. Verse 6 shows Isa presenting himself as a link confirming the Torah and foretelling Ahmad, the one who praises most before becoming the praised. He laments that abundant free knowledge goes unused. The fourth clause is that refusing to hand the legacy to the next generation is the worst oppression, since Islam lives through chains of transmission, as the memorized Quran shows. He asks everyone to learn enough to pass something on.

outline.heading: "Why do you hurt me?": Musa's complaint
outline.gist: Musa's struggle was his people's failure to follow; qad before a present-tense verb affirms that they knew he was the messenger.

outline.heading: Zaghu: cutting corners and swerving
outline.gist: When they took shortcuts off the straight path, Allah let their hearts swerve; zaygh and fisq both mean leaving a known path.

outline.heading: Prophetic ownership of the deen
outline.gist: Their deviation felt like a personal injury to Musa because he owned the message.

outline.heading: When I skip my part, I hurt you
outline.gist: A team or nation is an abstraction; failing your share harms every member, so the social contract makes us answerable to each other.

outline.heading: Small shortfalls add up
outline.gist: One person's neglect seems untraceable among two billion, but accumulated it explains decades of Muslim suffering; Allah traces every share.

outline.heading: Find what you can contribute
outline.gist: Teaching children Quran, driving elders, raising a family or giving monthly; only you know what you have to offer, and the strong Musa used "you hurt me" to remind them.

outline.heading: "We hear and disobey": haggling over the law
outline.gist: They wanted Musa to listen to their complaints and bring the commands down, like bargaining in a market.

outline.heading: Musa and the fifty prayers
outline.gist: On the Night Journey Musa urged the Prophet to return and ask for less, knowing his own people; Allah made five worth fifty.

outline.heading: Losing insight
outline.gist: You are safe as long as you can see your own faults; marriages end when neither side can, and a swerved heart cannot be guided.

outline.heading: Third clause: accept Islam as it is
outline.gist: You will not like every command; what matters is following because it is true and from Allah.

outline.heading: "We hear and obey", then voice your struggles
outline.gist: The right response accepts the truth fully and then asks for patience, help and time to change oneself.

outline.heading: Two approaches, and who may reinterpret
outline.gist: Falling short while acknowledging the law is safe; rewriting it to suit yourself is the problem, and only scholars with decades of training may challenge rulings.

outline.heading: The Sabbath nets
outline.gist: Unwilling to give up Saturday's catch, they cast nets on Friday and drew them on Sunday, finding a way around the law.

outline.heading: Preserving the law is on us
outline.gist: A law not accepted as it is gets lost even if its words remain, as with commands in the Bible few observe; no one aces it, but keep acknowledging what is right.

outline.heading: "Come as you are to Islam as it is"
outline.gist: Someone struggling with alcohol is welcome while acknowledging it is haram, but cannot demand Islam accommodate drinking in the masjid.

outline.heading: Isa: "I am the messenger of Allah to you"
outline.gist: Like Musa, Isa affirms his messengership because he is about to ask something of them.

outline.heading: One theology, different laws
outline.gist: All prophets brought the same belief and ethics while their laws differed, and that variation is wider than people think.

outline.heading: Abundant knowledge, little learning
outline.gist: Material on the biblical prophecies of Ahmad, once hard to find, is now free online, yet people prefer entertainment.

outline.heading: What is always available is taken for granted
outline.gist: As in relationships, free knowledge is undervalued while people pay for poor teaching; charging would turn service into a transaction, and he has no solution yet.

outline.heading: "This is clear magic": the oppression of lying about Allah
outline.gist: They dismissed the clear proofs; Allah does not guide the oppressors, as He does not guide those who deviate.

outline.heading: Carrying the baton
outline.gist: Do not refuse truth because it is new or unfamiliar to your culture; the final message can grow with time and place.

outline.heading: Fourth clause: refusing the legacy is the worst oppression
outline.gist: The next generation receives Islam only if this one hands it down; one generation's refusal severs the chain.

outline.heading: The chain of transmission
outline.gist: Millions have memorized the Quran through chains back to the Prophet, so burning every copy would lose nothing; hadith and scholarship pass teacher to student.

outline.heading: Ahmad before Muhammad
outline.gist: Ahmad means the one who praises most and Muhammad the one praised; he had to praise before being praised. Isa saw himself as one link in a chain.

outline.heading: Your share in handing Islam on
outline.gist: Learn enough to pass something down; avoid deviation and oppression, the two failures these verses name.

mTsSxLg0I6I.title: Surat As-Saff, Part 1 (Verses 1-4)
mTsSxLg0I6I.one_line: As-Saff 1-4: the social contract with your community begins with doing what you say and standing together in unbroken rows.
mTsSxLg0I6I.summary: He presents As-Saff as the Quran's social contract: what the individual owes the group, later framed as an actual contract in verse 10. He notes how strange and meaningful it is that Allah has us perform prayer, our most intimate act, shoulder to shoulder in straight rows, which the Prophet stressed in many narrations. The opening glorification reminds believers why they act, because means easily become goals and group loyalty can replace pleasing Allah, especially since people behave worse in groups than alone. Verses 2 and 3 condemn saying what you do not do as most hateful to Allah. He reads this as a problem of commitment rather than hypocrisy proper: the shahadah is a package that must be lived. He illustrates with Muslims who believe in equality yet race to Jumu'ah and quarrel outside the masjid, explaining that good values producing bad behaviour are hardest to fix, and cites a survey finding that the top reason Muslims leave Islam is the conduct of visibly religious people. True religiosity increases compassion. The first clause of the contract is commitment, since saying you lack time means it did not make your priority list. Verse 4 uses combat as the ultimate test: even in battle believers stand in solid rows, so unity and equality are the second clause, illustrated by Sawad at Badr.

outline.heading: Shorter surahs, condensed meanings

outline.heading: As-Saff as a social contract
outline.gist: After surahs on relationships within the group, this one addresses what the individual owes the group itself, presented as a contract.

outline.heading: Why pray our most intimate prayer in rows?
outline.gist: Private conversation with Allah is performed squeezed together in straight lines, so the group is present even in intimacy.

outline.heading: The Prophet aligning the lines of prayer
outline.gist: He walked the lines adjusting shoulders, and some twenty-five authentic narrations warn that crooked rows bring discord between hearts.

outline.heading: What we owe the community
outline.gist: Each element of the surah defines a part of the social contract.

outline.heading: Opening glorification: when means become goals
outline.gist: The Medinan surahs open with tasbih to remind you why you act; once salah or any act becomes the goal itself, the compass is lost.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz al-Hakim
outline.gist: He is beyond question and unstoppable, yet all-wise, so everything He commands serves you.

outline.heading: Act because Allah commands, not because everyone does
outline.gist: This liberates you; otherwise you defend your group simply because it is yours, without self-critique.

outline.heading: People behave worse in groups
outline.gist: Reasonable individuals turn hateful or reckless together, as he saw in a village and with young men; social contracts exist to curb this.

outline.heading: "Why do you say what you do not do?"
outline.gist: Allah calls it most hateful in His sight, using an intense word.

outline.heading: The shahadah is a package
outline.gist: Testifying that there is no god but Allah carries commitments; saying it and stopping is the problem.

outline.heading: Why dishonesty is so hurtful
outline.gist: People respect someone cruel but honest more than someone who professes love and keeps failing them; maqt is rare in the Quran, used also for marrying a father's wife.

outline.heading: Not hypocrisy but commitment
outline.gist: The verse targets failure to see through what you signed up for in time and money; if you cannot pray alone, you cannot do the rest alone.

outline.heading: When Allah pauses: "this is a big deal"
outline.gist: As with the slander of Aishah, verse 3 is a pause stressing what people think trivial.

outline.heading: Beliefs we all hold but do not live
outline.gist: Every Muslim claims to respect others and reject special treatment for himself.

outline.heading: The race to Jumu'ah and the blurred-video study
outline.gist: People quarrel outside the masjid to save seconds, and in a study subjects condemned their own blurred-out behaviour until shown it was theirs.

outline.heading: Tawhid means no ranks among creation
outline.gist: There is one God and everything else is creation, so no one is exempt from the rules; we have normalized behaviour our values reject.

outline.heading: Good values, bad behaviour: the hardest problem
outline.gist: A bad value can be corrected, but when a sound value coexists with bad conduct there is little to fix.

outline.heading: Why Muslims leave Islam
outline.gist: A survey of about six hundred American Muslims found the top reason was the behaviour of people who present themselves as religious.

outline.heading: More religion should mean more compassion
outline.gist: Mercy is a sensitive marker of religiosity; someone who loves Allah promises to bring His lost servant back, not drive him away.

outline.heading: First clause: commitment
outline.gist: You owe the group follow-through, present when needed and when not; the contract runs both ways.

outline.heading: Floaters and "I don't have time"
outline.gist: Lack of commitment is every community's greatest challenge; "no time" means it did not make your priority list, and deen and community must always make the cut.

outline.heading: Why combat is the Quran's example
outline.gist: Combat is the ultimate test of character, not a love of bloodshed; danger reveals who you are.

outline.heading: Straight rows even in battle
outline.gist: If lines matter when death is near, they matter more in prayer, because they embody unity and equality; many rows today are a mess.

outline.heading: Sawad at Badr
outline.gist: Tapped by the Prophet's stick for standing out of line, Sawad asked for retaliation, then embraced the Prophet so his skin would last touch his before dying.

outline.heading: Second clause: unity like a solid structure
outline.gist: You need not like each other to stand together; we declare our unity before every prayer, and it is the community's most important asset.

8:60.ar: وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُم مَّا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُم مِّن قُوَّةࣲ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلۡخَيۡلِ تُرۡهِبُونَ بِهِۦ عَدُوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ وَءَاخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُهُمۡۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تُظۡلَمُونَ
8:60.en: Make ready for them all thou canst of (armed) force and of horses tethered, that thereby ye may dismay the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others beside them whom ye know not. Allah knoweth them. Whatsoever ye spend in the way of Allah it will be repaid to you in full, and ye will not be wronged

8:3.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
8:3.en: Who establish worship and spend of that We have bestowed on them

9:111.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:111.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

8:36.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ لِيَصُدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ فَسَيُنفِقُونَهَا ثُمَّ تَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَسۡرَةࣰ ثُمَّ يُغۡلَبُونَۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ يُحۡشَرُونَ
8:36.en: Lo! those who disbelieve spend their wealth in order that they may debar (men) from the way of Allah. They will spend it, then it will become an anguish for them, then they will be conquered. And those who disbelieve will be gathered unto hell

8:37.ar: لِيَمِيزَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ بَعۡضَهُۥ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فَيَرۡكُمَهُۥ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيَجۡعَلَهُۥ فِي جَهَنَّمَۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
8:37.en: That Allah may separate the wicked from the good, The wicked will He place piece upon piece, and heap them all together, and consign them unto hell. Such verily are the losers

65:7.ar: لِيُنفِقۡ ذُو سَعَةࣲ مِّن سَعَتِهِۦۖ وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقُهُۥ فَلۡيُنفِقۡ مِمَّآ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُۚ لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا مَآ ءَاتَىٰهَاۚ سَيَجۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ عُسۡرࣲ يُسۡرࣰ ا
65:7.en: Let him who hath abundance spend of his abundance, and he whose provision is measured, let him spend of that which Allah hath given him. Allah asketh naught of any soul save that which He hath given it. Allah will vouchsafe, after hardship, ease

l7YdpV9Znx0.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 3: Preparation
l7YdpV9Znx0.one_line: The law of preparation in Al-Anfal: infaq means turning money, time and skill into strength for the ummah, asking only Jannah in return.
l7YdpV9Znx0.summary: He opens with how hard it is to act normal at work and through the holidays while the death toll in Gaza keeps rising and the world debates whether to ask for it to stop. After recalling last week's warning against materialism, he introduces the second law: preparation, putting forward every kind of strength you have, social, political, spiritual, academic and financial. Infaq comes from a root meaning to pass from one state into another: you transform what Allah gave you into energy for His cause. Time, not money, is your real capital. At the second pledge of Aqabah the Prophet asked the Ansar to give what they had, whether much or little, and offered only Jannah. As long as Muslims want anything but Jannah for giving everything, nothing will change. Allah bought our lives and wealth, and almost always He asks for far less than life, so claiming you would die for the cause while refusing a little money is self-deception. The disbelievers spend too, and Allah uses spending to separate the good from the rotten. Even a date counts, and he tells of the poor man who donated his honour by forgiving everyone. In the second khutbah, quoting 65:7, he says he is tired of arguing over small budgets in a wealthy community; change starts with a strong local community.

outline.heading: Hard to act normal while Gaza bleeds
outline.gist: It is hard to go to work, sleep or watch people enjoy the holidays as the blood count rises and the world debates whether Muslim blood is worth asking to stop spilling. This hurts Muslims and any human being who never expected this in the 21st century.

outline.heading: The series so far
outline.gist: Al-Anfal analyzes the day of Badr in about 25 points, reasons for failure and means of victory; he will cover nine or ten. Last week was the warning against materialism: once the ummah is consumed by consumerism there is no way back.

outline.heading: The law of preparation: every kind of strength
outline.gist: Preparation here is not behind-the-scenes planning but putting in all you can: every resource, specialty and expertise, held back from nothing. The strength in 8:60 covers social, political, spiritual, academic, communal and financial power.

outline.heading: Infaq as transformation
outline.gist: The root of infaq means something passing out of one state into another, as with a tunnel or a death. You take what Allah gave you, money, time, knowledge or influence, and turn it into energy for His cause, and He grows it for you until the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Time is the real capital
outline.gist: We give time more easily than money because we undervalue it. Money comes and goes a million times and no one remembers it; time is the actual capital you own and an hour gone never returns.

outline.heading: The believers spend from what We provide
outline.gist: After last week's warning about the extra, the surah describes the believers as those who spend from what Allah provides: take what He gives and transform it into energy for His deen and His ummah.

outline.heading: The pledge of Aqabah: give whatever you have
outline.gist: Six men, then twelve, then about 72 men and women came from Madinah. The Prophet framed it as a transaction, and the second of the five articles was to put forward what you have, whether a lot or a little.

outline.heading: Jannah, period
outline.gist: When they asked what they would get, he offered one word: Jannah. No stocks, ownership or recognition, and they were content with it.

outline.heading: Anything less than Jannah and nothing changes
outline.gist: As long as Muslims want any compensation besides Jannah for giving everything they have, nothing will change; it will only get worse, because this is how Allah designed the story.

outline.heading: Allah bought your lives; everything else is cheap
outline.gist: Allah purchased our lives and wealth for Jannah. Sometimes life is asked, as with the people of Badr, but almost always it is effort, time, advocacy and social or financial influence, which are cheap by comparison.

outline.heading: If you won't give a little, you won't give everything
outline.gist: Do not fool yourself that you would give your life if you cannot give a little money or time or put your name on the line. That makes no sense.

outline.heading: The disbelievers spend too
outline.gist: The other side spends everything to turn people from the way of Allah, then regrets it. Spending is how Allah separates the rotten from the good: where are you putting what you were given?

outline.heading: Even part of a date
outline.gist: The rotten is heaped together and thrown into Hell. The Prophet said give and Allah will give you, and protect yourself from the fire even with part of a date.

outline.heading: Giving for Tabuk
outline.gist: When the Companions were told to give for Tabuk, each brought what he could: a small measure of wheat, a few dates, a single date.

outline.heading: The man who donated his honour
outline.gist: A poor man with nothing at home offered his honour: he forgave everyone who had ever hurt him. The next morning the Prophet asked for him and he stood up afraid he had said something wrong.

outline.heading: Accepted: offer whatever you have
outline.gist: The Prophet told him his gift was accepted like everyone else's. Their attitude was to offer whatever you have, with no audit, and whatever is given for Allah returns in full.

outline.heading: Give from what Allah gave you
outline.gist: 65:7 says it all: the one with abundance gives from his abundance and the one with little gives from what he has. Allah asks no more than you can, and ease comes after hardship.

outline.heading: Tired of arguing over budgets
outline.gist: There is an abundance of wealth in the community, yet he is tired of arguing over a few thousand dollars to run programs and pay salaries. We lack neither wealth, expertise, youth nor numbers, perhaps only organization and the sense that giving is an obligation.

outline.heading: Change starts with a strong local community
outline.gist: Sending money overseas will not rebuild cities. A strong, organized community that supports itself and raises its youth with strong identity has a voice felt wherever people are mistreated. Nothing is missing and no one holds us back but us.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Infaq is the core of the law of preparation: transform money, time, knowledge and influence into energy for Allah's cause. Whatever you give, much or little, is accepted and returned in full.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Preparation means exhausting every resource and expertise in every domain of strength, social, political, spiritual, academic and financial, holding nothing back.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: The Prophet offered the Ansar only Jannah. Any other expected return, recognition, ownership or reward, means the ummah goes nowhere.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The first and second pledges of Aqabah, with the second article of the pledge being to give what you have, whether much or little.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: We give time more freely than money because we undervalue it, yet money comes and goes while time is the actual capital and never returns.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Companions at Tabuk gave a handful of wheat or one date, and a destitute man offered his honour by forgiving everyone who had wronged him; all was accepted.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: The community lacks nothing but the will to give; a strong, organized local community that educates its youth will have a voice felt wherever people are mistreated.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The rising blood count, sleeplessness and the world's debate over whether Muslim blood is worth asking to stop make it impossible to act normal.

quran.point: Prepare against them whatever strength you can: the law of preparation covers every kind of strength, and whatever you spend in Allah's way is repaid in full.
The believers spend from what We provide them: take what Allah gives and transform it into energy for His cause.
Allah bought the believers' lives and wealth in exchange for Jannah, so we are obligated to offer everything.
The disbelievers spend their wealth to block Allah's way, then it becomes their regret.
So Allah may separate the rotten from the good and heap the rotten together into Hell: where you spend shows which you are.
The wealthy give from their abundance and those with little from what they have; Allah asks no more than you can, and ease follows hardship.

hadith.gist: At the second pledge of Aqabah one article was to spend in hardship and in ease, whether you have much or little, and the only promised return was Jannah.
Give and Allah will give to you.
Protect yourselves from the fire even with half a date.

When charity was called for, Companions brought whatever they had, some a little wheat, some a single date; a poor man who had nothing announced he forgave everyone who had wronged him, and the Prophet told him the next morning his gift was accepted.

maxims: Infaq: turning what Allah gave you into energy
Time is the actual capital that you own
Jannah, period
If you can't give a little, you won't give everything
There's no audit: what do you have? Offer it
No one is holding us back but us

stories.who: The pledges of Aqabah
stories.point: Six, then twelve, then about 72 from Madinah pledged to give whatever they had; the Prophet offered nothing but Jannah, and they were satisfied.

stories.who: Companions giving for the Tabuk expedition
stories.point: Each gave what he could, a little wheat or a single date, and nothing was turned away.

stories.who: The poor Companion who donated his honour
stories.point: Having nothing, he forgave everyone who had hurt him as his charity; the Prophet announced it was accepted like everyone else's. Offer whatever you have.

contemporary: Gaza's rising death toll during the holiday season and the world's debate over a ceasefire
A wealthy London Muslim community that still argues over a few thousand dollars for programs and salaries
takeaways: Put forward every kind of strength you have, money, time, expertise and influence, for the ummah.
Seek only Jannah in return for what you give.
Give whatever you have, even a single date, or forgiveness if you have nothing else.
Stop haggling over small budgets; fund programs, salaries and youth education generously.
Start change locally by building a strong, organized community that supports itself.

39:22.ar: أَفَمَن شَرَحَ ٱللَّهُ صَدۡرَهُۥ لِلۡإِسۡلَٰمِ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورࣲ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦۚ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلۡقَٰسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مِّن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
39:22.en: Is he whose bosom Allah hath expanded for Al-Islam, so that he followeth a light from his Lord, (as he who disbelieveth)? Then woe unto those whose hearts are hardened against remembrance of Allah. Such are in plain error

39:23.ar: ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡحَدِيثِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مُّتَشَٰبِهࣰ ا مَّثَانِيَ تَقۡشَعِرُّ مِنۡهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُمۡ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمۡ وَقُلُوبُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡ هَادٍ
39:23.en: Allah hath (now) revealed the fairest of statements, a Scripture consistent, (wherein promises of reward are) paired (with threats of punishment), whereat doth creep the flesh of those who fear their Lord, so that their flesh and their hearts soften to Allah's reminder. Such is Allah's guidance, wherewith He guideth whom He will. And him whom Allah sendeth astray, for him there is no guide

94:1.en: Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate

6:125.ar: فَمَن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَهۡدِيَهُۥ يَشۡرَحۡ صَدۡرَهُۥ لِلۡإِسۡلَٰمِۖ وَمَن يُرِدۡ أَن يُضِلَّهُۥ يَجۡعَلۡ صَدۡرَهُۥ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجࣰ ا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَجۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:125.en: And whomsoever it is Allah's will to guide, He expandeth his bosom unto the Surrender, and whomsoever it is His Will to send astray, He maketh his bosom close and narrow as if he were engaged in sheer ascent. Thus Allah layeth ignominy upon those who believe not

5:15.ar: يَٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ قَدۡ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمۡ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا كُنتُمۡ تُخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَن كَثِيرࣲۚ قَدۡ جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ نُورࣱ وَكِتَٰبࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
5:15.en: O People of the Scripture! Now hath Our messenger come unto you, expounding unto you much of that which ye used to hide in the Scripture, and forgiving much. now hath come unto you light from Allah and plain Scripture

33:46.ar: وَدَاعِيًا إِلَى ٱللَّهِ بِإِذۡنِهِۦ وَسِرَاجࣰ ا مُّنِيرࣰ ا
33:46.en: And as a summoner unto Allah by His permission, and as a lamp that giveth light

24:35.ar: ۞ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشۡكَوٰةࣲ فِيهَا مِصۡبَاحٌۖ ٱلۡمِصۡبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوۡكَبࣱ دُرِّيࣱّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةࣲ مُّبَٰرَكَةࣲ زَيۡتُونَةࣲ لَّا شَرۡقِيَّةࣲ وَلَا غَرۡبِيَّةࣲ يَكَادُ زَيۡتُهَا يُضِيٓءُ وَلَوۡ لَمۡ تَمۡسَسۡهُ نَارࣱۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورࣲۚ يَهۡدِي ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَيَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلَ لِلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:35.en: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is as it were a shining star. (This lamp is) kindled from a blessed tree, an olive neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil would almost glow forth (of itself) though no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guideth unto His light whom He will. And Allah speaketh to mankind in allegories, for Allah is Knower of all things

57:12.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَسۡعَىٰ نُورُهُم بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۖ بُشۡرَىٰكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ جَنَّٰتࣱ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
57:12.en: On the day when thou (Muhammad) wilt see the believers, men and women, their light shining forth before them and on their right hands, (and wilt hear it said unto them): Glad news for you this day: Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein ye are immortal. That is the supreme triumph

24:40.ar: أَوۡ كَظُلُمَٰتࣲ فِي بَحۡرࣲ لُّجِّيࣲّ يَغۡشَىٰهُ مَوۡجࣱ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ مَوۡجࣱ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ سَحَابࣱۚ ظُلُمَٰتُۢ بَعۡضُهَا فَوۡقَ بَعۡضٍ إِذَآ أَخۡرَجَ يَدَهُۥ لَمۡ يَكَدۡ يَرَىٰهَاۗ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَجۡعَلِ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ نُورࣰ ا فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن نُّورٍ
24:40.en: Or as darkness on a vast, abysmal sea. There covereth him a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud. Layer upon layer of darkness. When he holdeth out his hand he scarce can see it. And he for whom Allah hath not appointed light, for him there is no light

17:1.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَسۡرَىٰ بِعَبۡدِهِۦ لَيۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡأَقۡصَا ٱلَّذِي بَٰرَكۡنَا حَوۡلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
17:1.en: Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship the neighbourhood whereof We have blessed, that We might show him of Our tokens! Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

50:16.ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ وَنَعۡلَمُ مَا تُوَسۡوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفۡسُهُۥۖ وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنۡ حَبۡلِ ٱلۡوَرِيدِ
50:16.en: We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein

2:74.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡمَآءُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَهۡبِطُ مِنۡ خَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:74.en: Then, even after that, your hearts were hardened and became as rocks, or worse than rocks, for hardness. For indeed there are rocks from out which rivers gush, and indeed there are rocks which split asunder so that water floweth from them. And indeed there are rocks which fall down for the fear of Allah. Allah is not unaware of what ye do

8:2.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُهُۥ زَادَتۡهُمۡ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
8:2.en: They only are the (true) believers whose hearts feel fear when Allah is mentioned, and when His revelations are recited unto them they increase their faith, and who trust in their Lord

12:18.ar: وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمࣲ كَذِبࣲۚ قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرࣰ اۖ فَصَبۡرࣱ جَمِيلࣱۖ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُسۡتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
12:18.en: And they came with false blood on his shirt. He said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience. And Allah it is Whose help is to be sought in that (predicament) which ye describe

12:85.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ تَفۡتَؤُاْ تَذۡكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوۡ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَٰلِكِينَ
12:85.en: They said: By Allah, thou wilt never cease remembering Joseph till thy health is ruined or thou art of those who perish

12:86.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡكُواْ بَثِّي وَحُزۡنِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
12:86.en: He said: I expose my distress and anguish only unto Allah, and I know from Allah that which ye know not

gkyYUmBhcnY.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Az-Zumar (39:22)
gkyYUmBhcnY.one_line: The chest opened to Islam and the hardened heart: Islam as a gift, walking by light, why sincerity needs love, and what hardens hearts.
gkyYUmBhcnY.summary: Verses 22 and 23 give the spiritual side of sincerity. 'Opening the chest' is figurative, as in the verse consoling the Prophet when revelation paused and the image of a chest tightening as if climbing into the sky; being Muslim is a gift Allah gave, not an achievement to boast of. Light from one's Lord means knowing where life leads: every blessing tests gratitude and every hardship tests patience, while others wander in darkness upon darkness. One cannot be sincere to someone one does not know or love, so a heart hard to Allah's remembrance cannot be sincere. Loving the unseen is difficult, but it comes from seeing that His withholding is also giving, that we are slaves to what we love, and through love of the Prophet, as Umar reasoned when he made him dearer than himself. Hardness of heart comes largely from long oppression that trickles down from rulers to homes, which is where harsh beating of children came from, and from shelving every pain until the heart shuts. Softness is not tears; it is letting truths reach the heart. Like Ya'qub, take your grief to Allah with beautiful patience, love Him even when He takes, and come to know Him through the Prophet's life, the Quran and creation.

outline.heading: Verses 22-23 recited, with a note on full assimilation
outline.gist: In 'fa-waylun lil-qasiyah' no trace of the nun remains in Hafs's reading.

outline.heading: The spiritual side of sincerity
outline.gist: Awareness of death from the previous verse is not enough; sincerity also needs the inner states these verses describe.

outline.heading: A question whose answer is understood
outline.gist: Is the one whose chest is opened better, or those hard of heart? The comparison is left implied by the context.

outline.heading: Sharh: an opening of the chest
outline.gist: Sharh means cutting open, as in anatomy; the image is figurative and common in Arabic speech and poetry.

outline.heading: Have We not opened your chest?
outline.gist: When revelation paused for months and Quraysh mocked him, the Prophet was troubled, and Allah reminded him that his chest had been opened to Islam.

outline.heading: A chest tight as if climbing into the sky
outline.gist: Al-An'am describes the one Allah leaves astray as feeling the tightness of thinning air: a real feeling behind a figurative image.

outline.heading: Islam is a gift, not an achievement
outline.gist: Our being Muslim is because Allah opened our chests; many Muslims do not find in Islam answers or what they need.

outline.heading: Light throughout the Quran
outline.gist: The Prophet as a lamp, the Book as light, Allah the light of the heavens and earth, and the believers' light running before them.

outline.heading: Walking on light: life is a test
outline.gist: Light is knowing where life leads; good tests gratitude and harm tests patience, so you move between the two until you meet Him pleased.

outline.heading: Darkness upon darkness
outline.gist: The Muslim knows what to do with wealth, power or illness; without light a person sinks so deep he cannot see his own hand.

outline.heading: You cannot be sincere to someone you do not know
outline.gist: Even knowing that sincerity matters is a favour that deserves a lifetime of gratitude.

outline.heading: Hearts hardened against remembrance
outline.gist: They feel no delight at hearing His name and praise, and are deprived of the most beautiful thing in this world.

outline.heading: No sincerity without love
outline.gist: In any relationship loyalty follows love; without some love of Allah, sincerity is impossible.

outline.heading: Why loving Allah is hard
outline.gist: We love what our senses reach and what resembles us, and we love only while we are given.

outline.heading: His withholding is a gift
outline.gist: The people of Allah felt safer when denied, reading it as a sign He still cared; the most tested are the prophets then the best after them.

outline.heading: You are a slave to what you love
outline.gist: Children make a man cowardly and stingy; the Prophet earned the title 'His servant' because he was enslaved by love of Allah.

outline.heading: Love of Allah: the highest truth in Islam
outline.gist: Nothing in Islam is higher than love of Allah, and sincerity is reached only through it.

outline.heading: Love of the Prophet: the gateway
outline.gist: He is human, so you can picture him and love him, and through his love for his Lord you come to love Allah.

outline.heading: Hearts harder than stone
outline.gist: Even stones split and let water flow; love of the Prophet is the easier door for a hardened heart.

outline.heading: Umar: dearer to me than myself
outline.gist: Umar left and returned having reasoned that alone he was headed for the Fire and with the Prophet for Paradise; great people move an idea quickly to the heart.

outline.heading: Hardness of heart deserves study
outline.gist: Believers' hearts tremble at Allah's mention; the Muslim peoples are believing societies, so hardness of heart is a serious problem.

outline.heading: Prolonged oppression hardens hearts
outline.gist: People oppressed for decades harden their hearts simply to survive.

outline.heading: Where harsh beating of children came from
outline.gist: Arabs and the early Muslims rarely hit children or wives; the culture of heavy beating came from oppression.

outline.heading: Oppression flows down into homes
outline.gist: Rulers wrong ministers, managers wrong employees, a man hits his wife and she hits the children, while those who plundered live in gentle comfort.

outline.heading: All hearts are alike
outline.gist: No people are born hard-hearted; the Prophet was wronged and stayed tender, so pain should soften you if understood rightly.

outline.heading: Softness of heart is not tears
outline.gist: A soft heart lets a truth pass straight from the mind into it; a closed heart hears 'we will die' and does not move.

outline.heading: Pains shelved until the door shuts
outline.gist: Review why your heart hardened: each unprocessed pain is put on a shelf until the heart closes; take pain back to Allah instead.

outline.heading: Ya'qub and beautiful patience
outline.gist: Losing his beloved young son, likely through his own sons, he still chose a patience that is accepting and content.

outline.heading: I complain of my grief only to Allah
outline.gist: Bathth is a pain that nearly kills; Ya'qub carried it to Allah rather than closing on it, and knew from Allah what others did not.

outline.heading: A sin that humbles you
outline.gist: A sin that leaves you broken before Allah is better than obedience that leaves you proud; Allah only asks that we return His love.

outline.heading: Love that only receives is not love
outline.gist: Prove you love Him while He withholds; Ibrahim could only carry out the command to sacrifice his son through love.

outline.heading: You cannot love whom you do not know
outline.gist: Know Allah through the life of the Prophet, His revealed words and the universe, and love will follow.
